card.name: The word a introducing an unnamed thing
card.fires_on: The article "a" (or "an", "a common") right before a vague noun that is about to be described or named, such as "a skin condition called" or "a substance that". It appears in medical and news text.

modes.label: Article before a described condition
modes.description: "a" opens an indefinite noun phrase that a later phrase will name or describe, such as "called ...".
modes.example: - Treating<< a>> skin condition in infants called atopic ec

modes.label: Article before a substance or place
modes.description: "a" or "a substance" introduces something only loosely identified, followed by "that" or a name.
modes.example: The source of the outbreak is<< a>> compounding pharmacy called New England Compounding

card.writes: It favors words meaning "a certain" or "a kind of" (including Chinese equivalents), which fits introducing something not yet named.
card.plain: It fires on "a" when the text is about to introduce a certain kind of thing and then describe or name it.
